t.E477.agn: In 2018 EFSA reconfirmed the ADI of 25 mg/kg body weight expressed as propane-1,2-diol (about 80 mg/kg body weight as E477). Because exposure estimates at the reported use levels did not exceed the ADI, it found no safety concern; it stated that it planned a combined evaluation of additives that are sources of propane-1,2-diol (E477, E1520, E405).
t.E477.body: Propane-1,2-diol esters are broken down in the digestive tract into propane-1,2-diol (propylene glycol) and fatty acids; in laboratory experiments this breakdown was not complete.
t.E477.eval: The fatty acid source may be vegetable or animal (including beef/pork); the source is often not stated on the label.
t.E477.prod: It is an emulsifier produced by esterifying propylene glycol with fatty acids or by transesterification with fats and oils.
t.E477.regx.0: Re-evaluated; ADI of 25 mg/kg body weight (as propane-1,2-diol), no safety concern at the reported uses.
t.E477.summary: An emulsifier produced from fatty acids. It is used in whipped cream and cake mixes.
t.E477.what: It is an emulsifier; it supports air retention and foam structure, especially in cake batters and whipped creams.
